scenarios.headline:
What does the voice
say in the morning?
scenarios.description:
Pick a topic and it chooses a line that fits the day.
All four are free.

items.title: “It might rain today. Don’t forget your umbrella when you head out.”
items.body: Clear, rain, snow, fine dust, heat or cold: the greeting matches the day.

items.title: “Time for your medicine. Take it now, before you turn off the alarm.”
items.body: Set it on a parent’s alarm and it reminds them every day. Nothing to write.

items.title: “Luck is on your side today. If there’s something you’ve been putting off, give it a light try.”
items.body: Enter a birth date once and hear the day’s reading every morning.

items.title: “You don’t have to do everything perfectly from the start. Begin with what you can do now, one thing at a time.”
items.body: For the hard weeks. A different line every day.

items.q: How do I make a voice?
items.a: Record something or upload an audio file. Recordings run from 12 seconds up to 2 minutes. If you don’t have a file, playing a video of that person and recording it works too. Once the voice exists, every line you write is read back in it, on as many alarms as you like. Adding a voice of your own needs a plan, and you can create one per month.

items.q: Does it ring in airplane mode or without internet?
items.a: Yes. Alarms use your phone’s own alarm scheduler and audio that was downloaded ahead of time. Nothing is asked of a server at ring time, so it works in airplane mode, underground, or with no data.

items.q: Do I still get snooze and weekday repeats?
items.a: Yes. Repeat days, snooze length and limit, vibration patterns, alarm sounds and skipping public holidays all work like any alarm app. The only difference is what you hear.

items.q: How far does my voice travel?
items.a: No further than the people on your Couple or Family plan. Groups are joined by invite code, and whoever receives a voice can only use it for alarms inside the app. There is no way to export the audio as a file.

items.q: What happens to my voice if I delete my account?
items.a: It is destroyed on our servers. If someone else has an alarm built from it, the voice is removed there too and the alarm falls back to an alarm sound. The alarm itself stays. The time is theirs.

items.q: Can I redo a voice I’m not happy with?
items.a: You can re-record as many times as you like before you confirm it. After that, you can register one voice per month, and deleting the one you made won’t give you another that month.

items.q: If I cancel, do I lose access right away?
items.a: No. Cancel in the store and you keep everything until the time you already paid for runs out. After that you move to the free plan, and alarms built from your own voice fall back to an alarm sound.

items.q: Are there forced missions, like math or photo challenges?
items.a: No. AlarmTalk is built around emotional waking, not forced waking. The goal is to wake up to a voice you genuinely want to hear.

Two groups. Fans who want to wake up to their favorite idol, voice actor, or character, and seniors and long-distance families who want their child, grandchild, or partner’s voice every morning. Both share one thing: a specific voice they want to hear daily.
Android is on Google Play now. The iOS app is being prepared for the App Store, and the App Store button on this page will open as soon as it’s live.

meta.title: Company
meta.description: AlarmTalk redefines an alarm not as a sound, but as a relationship. Our mission, our principles, and what we’re building.

hero.description: AlarmTalk redefines an alarm as a relationship instead of a sound. Starting every morning’s first second with a fresh line in a voice you love. That’s our single job.

principles.headline: Five principles we work by
principles.description: We are early, going from zero to one. That’s exactly why clear principles matter more, not less.

items.title: Build something people want every day
items.body: Not a one-time trick. The first thing people meet every morning.

items.title: Treat trust as the heaviest constraint
items.body: Voice cloning shares roots with voice phishing. Closed sharing and no-export are non-negotiable.

items.title: Emotion over force
items.body: Not a louder alarm. One you actually want to hear. We wake the mind, not just the body.

items.title: Ask for a 10× answer
items.body: We don’t chase 10% gains. We look for an answer that is 10× different: a third path beyond beeps and missions.

items.title: Build globally from day one
items.body: Not a Korea-only product. We assume a multilingual, multicultural user from the first commit.
